title: Take only the top plate off a pile in a destacking cradle, without disturbing the plates under it
instruction: Put only the top plate of the pile on the green pad, lying flat. Leave the other two plates stacked where they are.
context: Press and machine operators feed metal blanks one at a time from a pile; lifting two at once (a double blank) can damage the die, and knocking the pile out of its cradle stops the line. When guides leave no room for fingers beside the pile, the top sheet has to be slid out past the end of the pile before it can be gripped.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Plates (loose): three aluminium plates, 160 mm long, 80 mm wide, 12 mm thick, 415 g each; the top one is blue anodised, the two under it bare aluminium. They lie flat and stacked squarely with the long side running front to back: the pile spans 16.0 to 32.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 10.0 to 18.0 cm left of the midline, 0 to 36 mm high (bottom plate 0 to 12 mm, middle 12 to 24 mm, top 24 to 36 mm). Destacking cradle (fixed): two dark painted steel guide rails, each 160 mm long, 8 mm wide and 36 mm tall, running front to back over the same 16.0 to 32.0 cm as the pile, one on each side with 3 mm of clearance to the plates: the left rail spans 18.3 to 19.1 cm left of the midline, the right rail 8.9 to 9.7 cm. Both ends of the cradle are open. Pad (fixed): a green plastic sheet 200 mm front to back, 120 mm wide and 2 mm thick, spanning 14.0 to 34.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 27.0 to 39.0 cm left of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Every limit below is inclusive (a value exactly at a limit passes). At rest means moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s. A plate is flat when its faces are within 3 degrees of horizontal (either face up). Lower plates: the bottom and middle plates are intact when, at every moment of the trial, neither plate's centre has moved more than 3 mm from where it started and neither has tilted more than 3 degrees, and at the end both are at rest; this is judged over the whole trial, so lifting, dragging or pulling out a lower plate and putting it back still scores 0. The record is cleared only when the scene is reset to the starting layout (every plate back within 0.5 mm of its start in one jump of more than 20 mm), not by rebuilding the pile by hand. The cradle's lane is the strip 8.9 to 19.1 cm left of the midline (between the rails' outer faces), along the whole table, over the cradle and beyond both of its ends. Score 1.0: the blue top plate is flat and at rest, its whole outline (all four corners) lies within the pad's outline (1 mm of slack), and its underside is within 1 mm of the pad's top, with the lower plates intact. Score 0.5: the top plate is flat and at rest with its underside within 1 mm of the table or the pad top, no part of its outline is in the cradle's lane, and the lower plates are intact; this covers a plate set down on the table out of the lane, or turned or overhanging the pad. A plate pushed off either end of the pile without a grasp lands in the lane and scores 0. Score 0.25: the top plate is flat and at rest on the middle plate (underside within 1 mm of 24 mm high) with one end at least 40 mm past an end of the pile (at or beyond 36.0 cm in front of the arm bases, or at or nearer than 12.0 cm), and the lower plates are intact. Score 0 in every other case: the top plate on the pile less than 40 mm out, on the rails, in the cradle's lane on the table, tilted, on edge, held above any surface, moving or off the table; or a lower plate moved more than 3 mm or tilted more than 3 degrees at any time (for example both upper plates lifted together, the whole pile pushed, or a bare plate put on the pad), whatever the top plate's state. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Stack the three plates squarely between the rails, flush with the rail ends, long side front to back. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Every object is a rigid box. The plates are 12 mm thick, far thicker than typical 1 to 3 mm press blanks, so a finger can push the top plate's end without touching the plate below; real blanks also cling through oil films, which is not modelled (dry friction at the simulator's defaults, not measured). The cradle is two plain rails with no end stop, fanning magnets or air knives. Either face up counts as flat.
